title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Bahrain: Iran hit site; Hormuz tankers struck
preheader: Two tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz; Iran says it shot down a US drone.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Sunday, November 22, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 1 update on stories you're following and 7 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Bahrain says Iran struck industrial site as tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz
stories.why_important: Bahrain said Iran hit a civilian industrial site, and two tankers took hits in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it targeted US bases in Bahrain and shot down a US drone. The attacks end a lull in the US-Israel-Iran war and threaten a key oil route.
stories.what_overlooked: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said it targeted US bases at al-Riffa and Awali. It said the targets were not just a civilian site, and Bahrain reported no casualties.
stories.prediction: A third tanker strike within 72 hours would show Iran is targeting shipping, not just bases.

stories.story_title: Russian cargo ship hit by drones in Gulf of Finland, Finland tightens security
stories.why_important: Drones hit a cargo ship bound for Kaliningrad in open waters in the Gulf of Finland. Finland brought back air and sea restrictions and suspects a Russian chopper violated its airspace. The strike brings the Ukraine war into a NATO member's waters.
stories.what_overlooked: Finnish officials said Sparta II is on a US sanctions list and has ties to Russia's forces. That makes it a target in the war, not a random cargo ship.
stories.prediction: Finland will report on the suspected Russian chopper incursion within 72 hours; confirmation would raise NATO tensions.

stories.story_title: Eisenkot invites Netanyahu's Likud to Israeli coalition talks
stories.why_important: Gadi Eisenkot, set to form Israel's next government, invited Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud to power-sharing talks starting Sunday. October's vote left no clear winner, so a broad government could change policy on Iran and the Palestinians.
stories.what_overlooked: Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party said the talks aim at the 'broadest possible government'. Likud has not yet agreed to join, and the offer alone does not guarantee a power-sharing deal.
stories.prediction: Likud's response by Monday will show whether Netanyahu accepts a junior role in an Eisenkot-led government.

quick_hits.text: Mexico captured Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as El Chapo Isidro, in Sinaloa; 11 people died in the raid and shootout.
The FBI is investigating a breach of its National Crime Information Center, a database of criminal records; Trump downplayed the hack.
Myanmar's army-backed government called ASEAN's decision to deny it full representation at summits 'unfair and imbalanced'.
French protesters marched for a sixth weekend against high living costs, weak public services and police brutality.
The US Commerce Department barred data centers abroad with advanced American AI chips from serving customers in China, Iran and Russia.
Vice President JD Vance declined to endorse Trump's claim that Iran was close to a nuclear weapon before the US went to war.
US-Iran talks are deadlocked over uranium enrichment, TASS reported, citing Al Arabiya, with both sides holding firm despite mediators' proposals.

big_number.context: The EU proposed cutting €204 billion from its earlier budget plan while adding a 3% tax on major digital companies.

views.quote: Our position is clear: as long as Iran's demands are not met, the discussion on the Strait of Hormuz and its opening is pointless,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said

perspective_grid.blindspot: A severe storm in Tupancireta, Brazil, killed at least three people and damaged about 5,000 homes, with authorities investigating a possible fourth death. The disaster shows the danger extreme weather poses to communities outside the region.
